claims.text: The driver's own trace shows that the longest continuous period he held position inside the arrival radius was 185 seconds — the run from 18:49:35 to 18:52:40, on 20 fixes — and the only other in-geofence run was 170 seconds, from 18:44:45 to 18:47:35. Both fall short of the 300-second minimum dwell for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, and POL-NS-01 limb (c) makes 'held position inside that geofence for a continuous dwell of at least' that minimum a conjunctive condition of the anchor clause: the fee is chargeable only if all four limbs hold. The 300-second figure is reached only by adding the two runs to 355 seconds, which the derived arrival block does under the summation in POL-NS-06(i). That summation is a qualification on POL-NS-06's shortfall arithmetic — the clause that exists to refund the rider — and the rider's submission is that it cannot supply the continuous hold limb (c) demands. The rider's account that the driver 'never even stayed 5 minutes in one place' is literally what the trace records.

The rider's account of a car that was 'one moment at the bay, then he drive off, then come back, then drive off again' is admitted twice over. The trace places the driver outside the arrival radius for the whole interval 18:47:35 to 18:49:35 — 11 fixes, reaching 179.0 m from the pin — and the driver's own chat message at 18:47:50 says 'the marshal make me move, bus lane until 8pm. i go one round and come back same place ah'. For 120 seconds of the waiting window there was no vehicle at the bay, and the driver's last message, 'cannot wait already, cancelling sorry' at 18:52:30, shows he terminated the trip with no further attempt to locate the rider.

POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a qualifying traffic advisory was such that holding position was 'not lawfully possible'. The rider does not dispute that the advisory artifact is present and populated with type KERB_RESTRICTION, that its active window 17:00-20:00 covers the waiting period and that its geometry covers the pickup road; the rider's point is the condition itself. The derived limb block tests advisory presence, type, geometry, window and the 300 m leash and treats those as sufficient — it does not test whether holding was impossible — and this record shows the same driver holding the same kerb for 170 uninterrupted seconds from 18:44:45 with the restriction already in force. The summation on which the driver's arithmetic depends therefore does not rest on an established condition.

The counterparty's answer — that the rider 'replied she was coming down at 6.46 and never came' — is not an answer to this dispute. POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation fee where the effective dwell falls short of the minimum 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages', and POL-NS-01 limb (c) is a test of the driver's hold at the pickup, not of the rider's whereabouts. The rider's message of 18:46:20 was delivered at 18:46:21 and read by the driver at 18:46:35, so the driver knew she was on her way before he left the bay at 18:47:35.

The money in issue is the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee: the fare breakdown shows cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, every other line being zero because the trip was cancelled. If limb (c) fails, POL-NS-06 refunds that cancellation-fee line in full, and POL-GEN-03 defines that outcome as FULL_REFUND — the whole contested amount returned to the filing party, who here is the rider. The GREATER-of test in the fee schedule is a tie on this trip (LARGE_VENUE 4.00 against RYDE_X 4.00), so the reconciliation does not move the figure.

claims.text: POL-NS-01 is satisfied on its face. The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 2026-08-07T18:44:30+08:00 (limb (a)); no boarding event and no trip start is recorded, and the trip was terminated by the driver at 18:52:45 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is one of the three codes limb (d) recognises. Limbs (b) and (c) are addressed by the GPS trace below.

The pickup zone class is LARGE_VENUE on the trip record, not assumed, so the POL-NS-02 arrival radius for the test is 120 m and the POL-NS-01 minimum dwell is 300 seconds. Against that radius the driver's trace carries 40 qualifying in-geofence fixes out of 83 fixes at 100% coverage with zero sampling gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds — vastly more than the three consecutive in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires. Arrival under POL-NS-02 is therefore established, and limb (b) of POL-NS-01 is met.

The effective in-geofence dwell is 355 seconds, not the 185 seconds of the longest single run. POL-NS-06(i) expressly permits separate in-geofence intervals within one pickup attempt to be summed, and every condition of that limb is met on this record: the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00214-01 is present and populated with type KERB_RESTRICTION, its geometry covers the Orchard Turn pickup road, and its 17:00-20:00 active window covers the whole waiting period; and the driver's furthest point between the intervals was 179 m from the pin, inside the 300 m leash. Two intervals (170 s from 18:44:45 to 18:47:35, and 185 s from 18:49:35 to 18:52:40) sum to 355 seconds against the 300 second minimum — a surplus of 55 seconds. POL-NS-06's refund condition is therefore not triggered, and the fee stands under POL-NS-01.

The driver did not drift off to another job: the 120-second interval outside the radius was enforced, not chosen. At 18:47:50 — inside that interval — he messaged the rider that the marshal had moved him on because the bus lane runs until 8 pm, and that he would go one round and come back to the same bay; he was back inside the radius at 18:49:35 and held there until 18:52:40. That is precisely the situation POL-NS-06(i) was drafted for: a driver circling a no-stopping kerb in compliance with the law rather than abandoning the pickup, whose time should count.

The rider's false-arrival argument under POL-NS-05 fails. Nothing in the trace places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or at or above the 15 km/h motion threshold at the 18:44:30 marker: across the whole waiting window the greatest distance recorded is the 179 m excursion, and the first qualifying in-geofence fix follows the marker by 15 seconds, within one 10-second sampling interval. In any event POL-NS-05(iii) is explicit that a marker tapped marginally early does not by itself defeat the fee where the corrected dwell still meets the minimum — and on the corrected basis the dwell is 355 seconds, 55 seconds above the 300 second minimum — so POL-NS-01 governs.

The rider's own exonerating route under POL-NS-04 fails on two independent limbs. Limb (b): her only locating message is the 18:46:20 'ok coming down now', to which the driver replied at 18:47:50 — 90 seconds later, inside the 120-second window — so the unanswered-contact limb is not met. Limb (c): across 70 rider fixes the trace records zero qualifying fixes inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius, the rider's device sitting between 691 m and 717 m from the pickup pin throughout the waiting window. The rider was not at the pickup point.

POL-NS-03 is not the governing clause either. It addresses a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; the trace places this driver inside the 120 m arrival radius for two separate runs, so the wrong-entrance branch is never reached. The pin-ambiguity goodwill in limb (ii) is likewise unavailable: it requires trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more, and this trip records 1 registered pickup point.

The SGD 4.00 charged is the correct figure under fee_schedule.resolution_rule and is not a fare defect under POL-NS-08(d). The LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee is SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee is SGD 4.00; the greater of the two governs and is SGD 4.00, which is exactly the cancellation_fee line and the total_charged in the fare breakdown, so the fee charged reconciles with the schedule for this trip's zone class and vehicle tier.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 entitles the driver to 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee, being SGD 3.20, the residual 20 percent retained as the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 the limb requires, and 2 divided by 118 completed_trips_30d is 0.017, well below the 0.08 rate. Both limbs must fail for withholding, and neither does, so compensation is payable and is not withheld.

The driver's account is corroborated point by point by independent telemetry rather than resting on his own statement: arrived_at 18:44:30 matches the 18:44:31 system 'arrived' message; his 18:45:10 chat names the ION PHV bay; his 18:47:50 marshal message matches the sole off-geofence interval, which begins at 18:47:35; and the RIDER_NO_SHOW termination at 18:52:45 lands five seconds after the final in-geofence run ends at 18:52:40.

No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 is present, so this case is decidable on the merits rather than sent to a reviewer: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, not the 3 or more limb (d) requires, and both rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so limb (c)'s two-or-more-same-pair test is not met. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip.

This is a rider-filed dispute over a charge that is still on the ledger: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands, so the rider's claim for return of the SGD 4.00 fails and the charge remains as it is; the ruling value this case produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, because the case moves SGD 3.20 to the driver rather than nothing.

The 120-second gap between them was the driver being moved on by the marshal because of the Orchard Road bus-lane/kerb restriction, which the LTA advisory records as active 17:00-20:00 with no stopping or waiting and enforcement active. POL-NS-06(i) allows those two intervals to be added where the qualifying KERB_RESTRICTION advisory covers the pickup road and window and the driver stayed within 300 m of the pin; he stayed within 179 m. The combined dwell is 355 seconds, 55 seconds above the 300-second minimum. The rider's argument that the dwell must be one continuous 300-second block is not accepted because the specific accumulation rule in POL-NS-06(i) governs this situation; the driver's time counts. The trip record also shows a driver arrival event and a RIDER_NO_SHOW cancellation with no boarding, satisfying POL-NS-01. The rider's absence - the rider track places her device about 691-717 m from the pin, outside the 150 m radius - does not create a refund where the driver's own wait is verified. POL-NS-04 does not apply because the driver replied to the rider's 18:46:20 message at 18:47:50, within 120 seconds, and the rider was outside the presence radius. POL-NS-05 does not defeat the fee: there is no qualifying reading at the 18:44:30 marker showing the driver more than 300 m away or at 15 km/h or more, and in any event the corrected dwell meets the minimum. POL-NS-03 does not apply because the driver was inside the arrival radius, not merely within 400 m of it. The $4.00 charge is the correct figure under the fee schedule: the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. Under POL-NS-07 the driver is entitled to 80% of the $4.00 fee, $3.20, and the platform retains $0.80. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below 4, and 2/118 completed trips is 0.017, below 0.08. No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 applies, and no clause produces a referral. Confidence is 0.88.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the $4.00 no-show cancellation fee on trip TRP-00214 stands, and the driver is paid $3.20 out of it.

Why the charge stands. POL-NS-01 allows the fee only if all four limbs hold. Arrival is proved: the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 18:44:30, and the GPS trace EV-GPS-00214 contains 40 qualifying in-radius fixes inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, far more than the three consecutive fixes POL-NS-02 requires. The trip was ended by the driver at 18:52:45 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which limb (d) recognises. For the dwell limb the pickup is a LARGE_VENUE, so the minimum is 300 seconds. Driver, your trace does not show one continuous 300-second hold: the two in-geofence runs are 170 s (18:44:45 to 18:47:35) and 185 s (18:49:35 to 18:52:40). But POL-NS-06(i) lets those separate intervals be summed for this pickup because the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00214-01 is present and populated with type KERB_RESTRICTION, its 17:00-20:00 window covers the wait and its geometry covers the Orchard Turn pickup road, and you never went further than 179 m from the pin (inside the 300 m leash). 170 + 185 = 355 seconds, clearing the 300-second minimum by 55 seconds. That is exactly what the clause is for: a driver moved on from a bus lane who goes one round and comes back has that time counted.

Rider, your point that he 'never even stayed 5 minutes in one place' is factually correct about each single run and I have accepted it, but it is not the winning point: POL-NS-06(i) is the reason the fee is not refunded, because the lawfully-forced departure and return are added and the total passes the minimum. Your other routes do not work either. ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The SGD 4.00 no-show fee stands and the driver is paid SGD 3.20, being 80% of that fee.

THE CHARGE. The pickup was the ION Orchard PHV bay, a LARGE_VENUE, so the arrival radius is 120 m and the required hold is 300 seconds. The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 18:44:30, no boarding event, and a driver-cancelled trip at 18:52:45 with reason RIDER_NO_SHOW — POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are met. Limb (b) is met: the GPS trace (100% coverage, 83 fixes, maximum gap 0 s) places the driver inside the 120 m geofence from 18:44:45 on 40 qualifying fixes. Limb (c), the dwell, is what the rider disputes.

DWELL. The trace shows two stretches inside the radius: 18:44:45–18:47:35 (170 s) and 18:49:35–18:52:40 (185 s). The rider is right that neither stretch alone reaches 300 s and that the longest single hold was 185 s. But POL-NS-06(i) expressly allows those stretches to be summed where the driver left and returned without going more than 300 m from the pin and an LTA advisory of the KERB_RESTRICTION type covering the pickup road was in force. Both conditions hold here: the furthest point the driver reached between the two stretches was 179 m (inside the 300 m leash), and EV-ADVIS-00214-01 is a KERB_RESTRICTION on Orchard Road/Orchard Turn active 17:00–20:00, covering the whole waiting period, corroborated by the driver's own message at 18:47:50 that the marshal had moved him on. Summed dwell is 170 + 185 = 355 seconds, 55 seconds above the 300-second minimum. The rider's argument that a summed figure cannot satisfy POL-NS-01 limb (c)'s continuous hold is rejected: POL-NS-06 states how the effective dwell is computed, and its limb (i) is precisely the rule for a driver circling a no-stopping kerb — his time counts. The rider's narrower point, that the derived block did not separately test whether holding was 'not lawfully possible', fails on this record: the advisory itself says vehicles holding the kerb will be moved on, and the driver was in fact moved on.

ROUTES CONSIDERED AND REJECTED. POL-NS-04 (unanswered contact) fails twice over: the driver replied at 18:47:50, 90 seconds after the rider's 18:46:20 message, inside the 120-second window, and the rider's own track places her device 691–717 m from the pin throughout the waiting window with zero qualifying fixes inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE radius. POL-NS-05 (false arrival) does not fire: nothing places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or at 15 km/h or above at the 18:44:30 marker, and POL-NS-05(iii) preserves the fee where the corrected dwell meets the minimum anyway. POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance) is not reached: the driver was inside the arrival radius, and registered_pickup_points is 1, so no pin-ambiguity goodwill is available.

INTEGRITY AND ESCALATION. No POL-NS-08 impairment applies: clock skew is under 90 s, the trace has no gap above 120 s, the chat log's 5 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count, and the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee equals the fee schedule's greater-of figure (LARGE_VENUE SGD 4.00 against RYDE_X SGD 4.00). No POL-NS-09 trigger applies: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, both profiles show disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, rider no_show_disputes_30d is 1, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (2 no-show terminations in 30 days is below 4, and 2/118 = 0.017 is below 0.08).

OUTCOME. The fee was chargeable, so the rider's claim for return of the SGD 4.00 is not supported and the charge stands. Under POL-NS-07 the driver is compensated at 80% of the SGD 4.00 fee, i.e. SGD 3.20, with SGD 0.80 retained as the platform service fee. The ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and amount_sgd carries the same SGD 3.20. No clause in this case produces a referral.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this case is decided on the platform's own telemetry, and the driver's no-show fee stands.

Arrival and termination. The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 18:44:30 and the GPS trace (83 fixes, 100% coverage, no sampling gap, maximum gap 0 s) places the driver inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius on 40 qualifying fixes — far more than the three consecutive in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires — so arrival and POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) are met. No boarding is recorded, and the driver terminated the trip at 18:52:45 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed, so limb (d) is met.

The dwell the rider contests. The rider is right that the trace shows two separate in-geofence runs — 170 s (18:44:45–18:47:35) and 185 s (18:49:35–18:52:40) — and that neither run alone reaches 300 s. But POL-NS-06(i) expressly permits separate in-geofence intervals within a single pickup attempt to be summed where a KERB_RESTRICTION advisory covers the pickup road and the waiting window and the driver never travelled more than 300 m from the pin. Every condition is met here: LTA advisory ADV-20260807-014 is a bus-lane/kerb restriction in force 17:00–20:00 whose geometry covers the Orchard Turn pickup road, holding position there was not lawfully possible (the driver was moved on by the marshal at about 18:47, and his own chat message at 18:47:50 records it), and his furthest point between the runs was 179 m, inside the 300 m leash. The effective dwell is therefore 355 s against the 300 s minimum — a surplus of 55 s — so limb (c) holds and POL-NS-06's refund condition is not triggered. I answer the rider's contrary submission directly: the summation is a rule about how the dwell limb is measured, and it is what makes the driver's time at the kerb count.

The rider's other routes. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate her: the driver replied to her 18:46:20 message at 18:47:50, within the 120-second window, so limb (b) fails, and her device shows no qualifying fix inside the 150 m rider-presence radius, sitting 691–717 m from the pin throughout the waiting window, so limb (c) fails too. Her reading of POL-NS-06 ('whether or not the rider was present') is correct in itself but does not help her, because the clause is never reached. There is no false arrival marker under POL-NS-05: the greatest distance from the pin anywhere in the waiting window is the 179 m excursion, well under 300 m, and the first qualifying in-geofence fix follows the marker by 15 seconds. POL-NS-03 does not apply because the driver was inside the arrival radius, and the trip records 1 registered pickup point, so the pin-ambiguity goodwill is unavailable.

The money. The SGD 4.00 charged reconciles with the fee schedule: the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) are a tie, and the greater is SGD 4.00, matching the cancellation_fee and total_charged lines, so there is no fare-integrity defect. Under POL-NS-07 the driver is compensated at 80% of the fee: SGD 3.20 of SGD 4.00, with SGD 0.80 retained as the platform fee. The anti-farming check does not trip — 2 no-show terminations in 30 days is below 4, and 2 ÷ 118 completed trips is 0.017, below 0.08 — so compensation is paid and not withheld. No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is met (confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the trace and trip record do not contradict each other on arrival or dwell, the same-pair dispute counters are 0, the anti-farming check is clear, and no deciding artifact is impaired), and no clause produces a referral. No admissibility impairment was flagged on any artifact this ruling relies on. The rider's SGD 4.00 charge stands, and SGD 3.20 moves to the driver.

ledger.claim: The driver's own trace shows that the longest continuous period he held position inside the arrival radius was 185 seconds — the run from 18:49:35 to 18:52:40, on 20 fixes — and the only other in-geofence run was 170 seconds, from 18:44:45 to 18:47:35. Both fall short of the 300-second minimum dwell for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, and POL-NS-01 limb (c) makes 'held position inside that geofence for a continuous dwell of at least' that minimum a conjunctive condition of the anchor clause: the fee is chargeable only if all four limbs hold. The 300-second figure is reached only by adding the two runs to 355 seconds, which the derived arrival block does under the summation in POL-NS-06(i). That summation is a qualification on POL-NS-06's shortfall arithmetic — the clause that exists to refund the rider — and the rider's submission is that it cannot supply the continuous hold limb (c) demands. The rider's account that the driver 'never even stayed 5 minutes in one place' is literally what the trace records.

The rider's account of a car that was 'one moment at the bay, then he drive off, then come back, then drive off again' is admitted twice over. The trace places the driver outside the arrival radius for the whole interval 18:47:35 to 18:49:35 — 11 fixes, reaching 179.0 m from the pin — and the driver's own chat message at 18:47:50 says 'the marshal make me move, bus lane until 8pm. i go one round and come back same place ah'. For 120 seconds of the waiting window there was no vehicle at the bay, and the driver's last message, 'cannot wait already, cancelling sorry' at 18:52:30, shows he terminated the trip with no further attempt to locate the rider.

POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a qualifying traffic advisory was such that holding position was 'not lawfully possible'. The rider does not dispute that the advisory artifact is present and populated with type KERB_RESTRICTION, that its active window 17:00-20:00 covers the waiting period and that its geometry covers the pickup road; the rider's point is the condition itself. The derived limb block tests advisory presence, type, geometry, window and the 300 m leash and treats those as sufficient — it does not test whether holding was impossible — and this record shows the same driver holding the same kerb for 170 uninterrupted seconds from 18:44:45 with the restriction already in force. The summation on which the driver's arithmetic depends therefore does not rest on an established condition.

The counterparty's answer — that the rider 'replied she was coming down at 6.46 and never came' — is not an answer to this dispute. POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation fee where the effective dwell falls short of the minimum 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages', and POL-NS-01 limb (c) is a test of the driver's hold at the pickup, not of the rider's whereabouts. The rider's message of 18:46:20 was delivered at 18:46:21 and read by the driver at 18:46:35, so the driver knew she was on her way before he left the bay at 18:47:35.

The money in issue is the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee: the fare breakdown shows cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, every other line being zero because the trip was cancelled. If limb (c) fails, POL-NS-06 refunds that cancellation-fee line in full, and POL-GEN-03 defines that outcome as FULL_REFUND — the whole contested amount returned to the filing party, who here is the rider. The GREATER-of test in the fee schedule is a tie on this trip (LARGE_VENUE 4.00 against RYDE_X 4.00), so the reconciliation does not move the figure.

POL-NS-01 is satisfied on its face. The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 2026-08-07T18:44:30+08:00 (limb (a)); no boarding event and no trip start is recorded, and the trip was terminated by the driver at 18:52:45 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is one of the three codes limb (d) recognises. Limbs (b) and (c) are addressed by the GPS trace below.

The pickup zone class is LARGE_VENUE on the trip record, not assumed, so the POL-NS-02 arrival radius for the test is 120 m and the POL-NS-01 minimum dwell is 300 seconds. Against that radius the driver's trace carries 40 qualifying in-geofence fixes out of 83 fixes at 100% coverage with zero sampling gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds — vastly more than the three consecutive in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires. Arrival under POL-NS-02 is therefore established, and limb (b) of POL-NS-01 is met.

The effective in-geofence dwell is 355 seconds, not the 185 seconds of the longest single run. POL-NS-06(i) expressly permits separate in-geofence intervals within one pickup attempt to be summed, and every condition of that limb is met on this record: the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00214-01 is present and populated with type KERB_RESTRICTION, its geometry covers the Orchard Turn pickup road, and its 17:00-20:00 active window covers the whole waiting period; and the driver's furthest point between the intervals was 179 m from the pin, inside the 300 m leash. Two intervals (170 s from 18:44:45 to 18:47:35, and 185 s from 18:49:35 to 18:52:40) sum to 355 seconds against the 300 second minimum — a surplus of 55 seconds. POL-NS-06's refund condition is therefore not triggered, and the fee stands under POL-NS-01.

The driver did not drift off to another job: the 120-second interval outside the radius was enforced, not chosen. At 18:47:50 — inside that interval — he messaged the rider that the marshal had moved him on because the bus lane runs until 8 pm, and that he would go one round and come back to the same bay; he was back inside the radius at 18:49:35 and held there until 18:52:40. That is precisely the situation POL-NS-06(i) was drafted for: a driver circling a no-stopping kerb in compliance with the law rather than abandoning the pickup, whose time should count.

The rider's false-arrival argument under POL-NS-05 fails. Nothing in the trace places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or at or above the 15 km/h motion threshold at the 18:44:30 marker: across the whole waiting window the greatest distance recorded is the 179 m excursion, and the first qualifying in-geofence fix follows the marker by 15 seconds, within one 10-second sampling interval. In any event POL-NS-05(iii) is explicit that a marker tapped marginally early does not by itself defeat the fee where the corrected dwell still meets the minimum — and on the corrected basis the dwell is 355 seconds, 55 seconds above the 300 second minimum — so POL-NS-01 governs.

The rider's own exonerating route under POL-NS-04 fails on two independent limbs. Limb (b): her only locating message is the 18:46:20 'ok coming down now', to which the driver replied at 18:47:50 — 90 seconds later, inside the 120-second window — so the unanswered-contact limb is not met. Limb (c): across 70 rider fixes the trace records zero qualifying fixes inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius, the rider's device sitting between 691 m and 717 m from the pickup pin throughout the waiting window. The rider was not at the pickup point.

POL-NS-03 is not the governing clause either. It addresses a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; the trace places this driver inside the 120 m arrival radius for two separate runs, so the wrong-entrance branch is never reached. The pin-ambiguity goodwill in limb (ii) is likewise unavailable: it requires trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more, and this trip records 1 registered pickup point.

The SGD 4.00 charged is the correct figure under fee_schedule.resolution_rule and is not a fare defect under POL-NS-08(d). The LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee is SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee is SGD 4.00; the greater of the two governs and is SGD 4.00, which is exactly the cancellation_fee line and the total_charged in the fare breakdown, so the fee charged reconciles with the schedule for this trip's zone class and vehicle tier.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 entitles the driver to 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee, being SGD 3.20, the residual 20 percent retained as the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 the limb requires, and 2 divided by 118 completed_trips_30d is 0.017, well below the 0.08 rate. Both limbs must fail for withholding, and neither does, so compensation is payable and is not withheld.

The driver's account is corroborated point by point by independent telemetry rather than resting on his own statement: arrived_at 18:44:30 matches the 18:44:31 system 'arrived' message; his 18:45:10 chat names the ION PHV bay; his 18:47:50 marshal message matches the sole off-geofence interval, which begins at 18:47:35; and the RIDER_NO_SHOW termination at 18:52:45 lands five seconds after the final in-geofence run ends at 18:52:40.

No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 is present, so this case is decidable on the merits rather than sent to a reviewer: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, not the 3 or more limb (d) requires, and both rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so limb (c)'s two-or-more-same-pair test is not met. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip.

This is a rider-filed dispute over a charge that is still on the ledger: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands, so the rider's claim for return of the SGD 4.00 fails and the charge remains as it is; the ruling value this case produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, because the case moves SGD 3.20 to the driver rather than nothing.
